;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Libya–Tunisia relations]]
**[[Tunisia]]'s [[Ministry of Defence (Tunisia)|Ministry of Defence]] says that a pilot is arrested after a damaged [[Libya]]n warplane, reported to be a [[Aero L-39 Albatros|L-39 Albatros]], makes an emergency landing on a road near the southern town of [[Beni Khadash]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-libya-security-tunisia/libyan-warplane-makes-emergency-landing-on-road-in-southern-tunisia-idUKKCN1UH13O (Reuters)]
*[[Suicide bomber]]s attack a French military base in [[Gao]], [[Mali]], where Estonian, French and Malian troops serve. Six Estonians and "around the same number" of French personnel are wounded in the attack. [https://news.err.ee/963913/six-estonian-defence-forces-members-injured-in-mali-terrorist-attack (ERR)]
*[[July 2019 Mogadishu bombing]]
**A bomb kills 17 people and injures 28 others in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2019/07/22/world/africa/22reuters-somalia-security.html (''New York Times'')] 

;Arts and culture
*''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' reports that [[Lil Nas X]] tied the all-time record on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] with his song "[[Old Town Road]]", as it spends its sixteenth week atop the chart; the other record-holders are [[Mariah Carey]] and [[Boyz II Men]] with "[[One Sweet Day]]", and [[Luis Fonsi]] with "[[Despacito]]" featuring [[Daddy Yankee]]. The song broke the record the next week. [https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/chart-beat/8523187/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-hot-number-one-hot-100-16th-week (Billboard)]

;Business and economy
*Due to declining sales, American retailer [[GNC (store)|GNC]] announces it will close between 700 and 900 stores. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2019/07/22/gnc-store-closings-up-900-could-close-focus-mall-stores/1800287001/ (''USA Today'')]

;International relations
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**The [[Iranian government]] announces the arrest of 17 citizens in the last months who are accused of spying in favour of the [[CIA]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/iran-claims-it-dismantled-cia-spy-ring-sentencing-some-to-death/a-49689687 (DW)]
*[[Russia–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea|South Korean]] fighter jets fire warning shots at three [[Russia|Russian]] planes as a reaction to an alleged violation of the country's [[national airspace]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-fires-warning-shots-at-russian-military-aircraft-in-its-airspace/a-49708651 (DW)]
*[[Foreign relations of Venezuela]]
**Four months after being expelled from the country, German Ambassador to Venezuela {{ill|Daniel Kriener|de}} returns to his post in the nation. [https://www.voanews.com/europe/german-ambassador-returns-venezuela (VOA)]
*[[Holy See–Syria relations]]
**[[Pope Francis]] petitions President [[Bashar al-Assad]] Assad to protect weak and defenseless in [[Syria]]. The pope’s appeal is in a letter to Assad delivered by Cardinal [[Peter Turkson]], prefect of the [[Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development]] at a meeting with the president in [[Damascus]]. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/pope-francis-petitions-assad-to-protect-weak-and-defenseless-in-syria-19933 (Catholic News Agency)]

;Law and crime
*A shooting in the town of [[Wächtersbach]], [[Hesse]], [[Germany]] gravely injures an [[Eritreans in Germany|Eritrean]] man. The suspect commits [[suicide]] after fleeing the scene. Police treat the incident to be inspired by [[xenophobia]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/eritrean-survives-shooting-in-germany-by-suspected-neo-nazi/a-49709540 (DW)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Haitian protests]]
**[[Haiti]]an [[Prime Minister of Haiti|Prime Minister]] [[Jean-Michel Lapin]], who was appointed 4 months ago, resigns amidst renewed protests. President [[Jovenel Moïse]] appoints {{ill|Fritz-William Michel|fr}} as the new Prime Minister. [https://www.telesurenglish.net/news/Haiti-officials-Announce-PM-Lapin-Resigned-20190722-0022.html (teleSUR)]
*Hundreds of followers from the Shia group Islamic Movement for Nigeria were out on the streets in [[Abuja]] to demand the release of their leader Sheikh [[Ibrahim Zakzaky]], who has been detained since 2015. Police opened fire and killed eleven protesters and a journalist. A police officer was also killed in the fight. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-africa-49067962?ns_mchannel=social&ns_source=twitter&ns_campaign=bbc_live&ns_linkname=5d368bfeef0ce9067bfed072%26Stray%20bullet%20kills%20Nigerian%20journalist%20covering%20clashes%262019-07-23T04%3A29%3A45.540Z&ns_fee=0&pinned_post_locator=urn:asset:53fdef21-79a2-4c5d-af77-f1ba8c3efae8&pinned_post_asset_id=5d368bfeef0ce9067bfed072&pinned_post_type=share (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*The [[Indian Space Research Organization]] successfully launches [[Chandrayaan-2]] to survey [[lunar water]] from [[Satish Dhawan Space Center]], [[India]]'s second [[lunar exploration]] mission. If successful, Chandrayaan-2 will become the first spacecraft to land on the [[lunar south pole]]. [https://www.firstpost.com/tech/science/chandrayaan-2-a-step-by-step-look-at-the-47-day-journey-after-its-spectacularly-successful-launch-7035951.html (FP)]
